You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From b0e03950dd71315204c24a3dffb2d9fc477e82de Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2021 14:51:43 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] stmmac: dwmac-loongson: fix uninitialized variable in
 loongson_dwmac_probe()

The "mdio" variable is never set to false.  Also it should be a bool
type instead of int.

Fixes: 30bba69d7db4 ("stmmac: pci: Add dwmac support for Loongson")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
---
 drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac-loongson.c | 3 ++-
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac-loongson.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac-loongson.c
index 8cd4e2e8ec40..e108b0d2bd28 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac-loongson.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac-loongson.c
@@ -49,7 +49,8 @@ static int loongson_dwmac_probe(struct pci_dev *pdev, const struct pci_device_id
 {
 	struct plat_stmmacenet_data *plat;
 	struct stmmac_resources res;
-	int ret, i, mdio;
+	bool mdio = false;
+	int ret, i;
 	struct device_node *np;
 
 	np = dev_of_node(&pdev->dev);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The "mdio" variable was declared as an integer but was never initialized, leading to potential use of an uninitialized variable in the function `loongson_dwmac_probe()`. This could result in undefined behavior depending on the value that "mdio" held at runtime. The patch corrects this by changing the type of "mdio" to a boolean and initializing it to false, ensuring it has a defined value before use.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    Code statements:
    <text1>

    <textN>

Root cause:
The "mdio" variable was declared as an integer but was never initialized, leading to potential use of an uninitialized variable in the function `loongson_dwmac_probe()`. This could result in undefined behavior depending on the value that "mdio" held at runtime. The patch corrects this by changing the type of "mdio" to a boolean and initializing it to false, ensuring it has a defined value before use.
